# External validation

Engine `mrgym-engine-0.3.0`. What this page is: the scanner compared with things it does not share code with, rung by rung. What it is not: a comparison with a measurement. Those are on their own page, [measured.md](measured.md) (rungs L4 and L5): public phantom sessions on real scanners against the engine's model of the same protocol, with the differences that were found. Nothing on either page shows that a protocol found on this scanner is right on a real one. The column "written by the authors" says who wrote the reference: a row whose reference the authors of MR Gym wrote shows that two programs solve the same equations, and is called verification here, not validation.

Regenerate: `python tools/external/run_all.py --write`. Check: `python tools/external/run_all.py --check`.

## L1. The scanner's equations, solved by other code

| # | Quantity | Reference | Reference written by the authors of MR Gym? | Cases | Largest difference | Tolerance | |
|---|---|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| L1.1 | RF-spoiled steady state of spgr and afi (hard pulses, no diffusion) | independent_bloch.spoiled_gre: 2,048 isochromats over one spoiler cycle, 3 x 3 rotations, time stepping from equilibrium | yes | 7 | 3.3e-12 M0 | ≤ 1e-06 | pass |
| L1.2 | rotation made by the windowed-sinc pulse at every position through the slice (Cayley-Klein parameters), 10 to 180 degrees, time-bandwidth 2 / 4 / 8 | independent_bloch.shaped_pulse acting on the three unit vectors, sample by sample | yes | 12 | 8.3e-12  | ≤ 1e-09 | pass |
| L1.3 | RF-spoiled gradient echo integrated over the slice (time-bandwidth 2 / 4 / 8) | independent_bloch.slice_gre: isochromats over (position through the slice) x (96 spoiler phases), the 128-sample pulse stepped under its slice gradient for each of them in every repetition | yes | 3 | 6.8e-06 relative | ≤ 0.001 | pass |
| L1.4 | spin echo and inversion recovery integrated over the slice: shaped 90 and 180 degree pulses, crushers, B1 80 to 115 % | independent_bloch.slice_se: isochromats over (position) x (32 crusher phases), both pulses stepped under their gradients; the longitudinal magnetisation is averaged over the crusher phases after every echo, as the scanner's model states | yes | 5 | 1.1e-10 relative | ≤ 0.001 | pass |
| L1.5 | balanced SSFP against off-resonance (hard pulses, 41 precession angles per TR; RF phase advance 180, 90 and 300 degrees per TR) | independent_bloch.bssfp: time stepping to the steady state, the phase turning the axis of every pulse | yes | 205 | 1.5e-09 M0 | ≤ 1e-06 | pass |
| L1.6 | inversion time that nulls an inversion-recovery spin echo at finite TR and inversion efficiency 0.85 to 1 | independent_bloch.ir_null: the longitudinal chain stepped through 40 repetitions, bisection | yes | 4 | 2.9e-08 relative | ≤ 1e-06 | pass |
| L1.7 | slice gradient of the three selective pulses, in nominal bandwidths across the prescribed thickness (1.197 / 0.994 / 1.000) | independent_bloch.slice_calibration: the width at half maximum of the transverse magnetisation that a 0.0001 degree pulse leaves on single isochromats, by bisection | yes | 3 | 1.7e-13 relative | ≤ 1e-06 | pass |
| L1.8 | RF-spoiled steady state with a saturation pulse (Mz x q, 6.5 to 8 ms before every excitation; 50 to 100 % saturated) | independent_bloch.spoiled_gre with the saturation as a step of the time stepping: 1,024 isochromats | yes | 5 | 3.1e-13 of the unsaturated signal | ≤ 1e-06 | pass |

L1.3: With T1 / T2 relaxation during a 2 ms pulse, which the scanner's model leaves out, the same integrator gives a signal 0.05 % away (20 degrees, TR 20 ms, T1 400 ms, T2 50 ms): a declared difference, not a tolerance.
L1.4: A refocusing pulse that is not 180 degrees everywhere stores a grating of longitudinal magnetisation, which identical crushers recall in the next repetition (a stimulated echo). The scanner's model leaves it out. With the grating kept, the same integrator gives -2 to +39 % of the served signal in these 5 cases (TR 300 to 2000 ms, T1 500 to 1200 ms): a declared difference, not a tolerance.
L1.8: The saturation acts on the longitudinal magnetisation only, in the scanner and in the integrator: what a real pulse does to the transverse magnetisation of earlier repetitions is left out of both (limits.md, block 9a).

Not run: per-pulse transient of the first 300 pulses: the scanner serves the periodic state only.

## L2. Another group's code

| # | Quantity | Reference | Reference written by the authors of MR Gym? | Cases | Largest difference | Tolerance | |
|---|---|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| L2.1 | RF-spoiled steady state of spgr (7 cases) and afi, dual TR (2 cases), no diffusion | sycomore 1.3.2 (Lamy and others), values stored 2026-11-25 | no | 9 | 1.7e-12 M0 | ≤ 1e-10 | pass |
| L2.2 | the same with diffusion: spgr (6 cases), afi (2 cases) | sycomore 1.3.2 (Lamy and others), values stored 2026-11-25 | no | 8 | 3.6e-10 M0 | ≤ 1e-07 | pass |

L2.2: Both codes use the constant-gradient b-factors of Weigel 2010: this checks the implementation, not the diffusion model.
sycomore on the machine that generated this page: not installed here: the stored values were used.

Not run: the pulse's Cayley-Klein parameters against sigpy.mri.rf.sim.abrm (sigpy is not installed here); an image of the flat QA world against MRzero-Core or KomaMRI (neither is installed here).

L3.4: The scanner counts the RF phase per raster position of period TR1; a published per-pulse increment of 39 degrees corresponds to about 46 degrees here. The instrument datasheet says so.

## Not checked against anything external

- contrast of `se` and `ir` in tissue beyond the null point and the slice integral (the tissue values decide it; the curves of `se` and `ir` on phantoms are compared with measurements in [measured.md](measured.md), rungs M7 and M9)
- the transient of every sequence (not served)
- the Nyquist-ghost model of `epi`
- fat saturation (efficiency, band, offset)
- the diffusion model itself (sycomore uses the same b-factor formula)
- the periodic-motion model beyond the position and amplitude of its ghosts
- the 3D mode (it is the hard-pulse signal with a price; slab profile and slab wrap are not modelled)

Tissue values and console timing left this list: both are compared in [measured.md](measured.md) (rungs M5 and M0).

The largest differences are from the machine that generated this page; values at rounding level differ between machines, the tolerances do not.
